title: Language models: mechanisms, training and evidence
summary: 48 detailed lessons on how language models work, from token probabilities and causal attention to Transformers, adaptation, efficient attention, expert routing and exact decoding mechanisms.
north_star: Explain what each language-model component computes, test its information boundary and make a scoped system decision from reproducible evidence.

stages.title: Compute the mechanism and challenge the claim
stages.outcome: Trace token probabilities, tokenization, attention and a count baseline with NumPy.

stages.title: Train and inspect a tiny transformer
stages.outcome: Build one bounded PyTorch decoder and prove mask, loss, split, restart and cache contracts.

stages.title: Evaluate adaptation and complete language systems
stages.outcome: Assess adaptation, retrieval, tools and reliability without conflating a small test with a safety guarantee.

lessons.title: Language-model claims and evaluation units
lessons.outcome: Separate predicting tokens from evidence of knowledge, reasoning or reliability.
lessons.lab: Label six statements as architectural, empirical or unsupported; define a token, document and task as distinct evaluation units.
lessons.verification: Every claim names its measurement unit and a counterexample; a fluent answer alone is not marked as a correctness test.

lessons.title: Scores, stable softmax and probability mass
lessons.outcome: Convert finite scores into a stable categorical distribution with an explicit axis.
lessons.lab: Compute softmax for [0,0] and [1000,1000], subtracting the maximum before exponentiation; try an invalid all-masked row.
lessons.verification: Both finite score vectors produce [0.5,0.5] within 1e-12; an all-masked row must be rejected instead of returning NaN.

lessons.title: Conditional probability and a sequence likelihood
lessons.outcome: Expand a sequence probability without treating tokens as independent.
lessons.lab: Use a fixed conditional table with probabilities 0.5,0.25,0.8 and calculate the product and negative log probability.
lessons.verification: Sequence probability=0.1 and total negative log likelihood=log(10) within 1e-12; changing a prefix may change the next conditional.

lessons.title: A count-based next-token baseline
lessons.outcome: Fit and inspect a tiny bigram model before adding neural machinery.
lessons.lab: Count transitions in fixed local token sequences; apply a declared add-one smoothing policy using training counts only.
lessons.verification: Every conditional row sums to 1; an unseen context follows the declared uniform fallback, and validation text never changes the counts.

lessons.title: Cross entropy, perplexity and denominator traps
lessons.outcome: Compute token loss and compare models only under compatible tokenization and scoring units.
lessons.lab: Average NLL for target probabilities [0.5,0.25], then compare document-weighted and token-weighted averages for unequal lengths.
lessons.verification: Mean NLL=1.5*log(2), perplexity=2**1.5 within 1e-12. Report token count; perplexity across different tokenizers is not a direct ranking.

lessons.title: Unicode, bytes and tokenizer round trips
lessons.outcome: Trace text through a reversible representation without confusing characters and bytes.
lessons.lab: Encode fixed ASCII, accented and emoji strings as UTF-8; retain exact bytes while comparing NFC normalization as an explicit data policy.
lessons.verification: Every input round-trips byte-for-byte when normalization is off. The chosen normalization changes identity deliberately and is recorded before splitting.

lessons.title: A tiny train-only subword vocabulary
lessons.outcome: Learn deterministic merge rules without leaking evaluation text into a tokenizer.
lessons.lab: Implement a small BPE merge table with a declared lexical tie-break on a local training fixture; freeze vocabulary before encoding validation.
lessons.verification: Tied pairs choose the same merge after a fresh run. Validation-only strings cannot change the vocabulary hash or merge count.

lessons.title: Embedding lookup is a learned table
lessons.outcome: Map token IDs to rows and track the feature axis independently of vocabulary size.
lessons.lab: Index a fixed 4x2 embedding table with IDs [2,0,2]; compare repeated-token rows and an out-of-range ID.
lessons.verification: Output shape=(3,2); first and third rows match exactly. ID 4 is rejected under the four-entry vocabulary.

lessons.title: Causal attention and prefix invariance
lessons.outcome: Prove that a query cannot use later token positions and diagnose a mask that only looks plausible.
lessons.lab: Implement scaled dot-product attention on fixed 3x2 Q/K/V arrays and test each prefix independently.
lessons.verification: Equal-logit causal outputs are [[2,0],[1,1],[8/3,8/3]] within 1e-12; arbitrary future-only changes leave earlier outputs invariant.

lessons.title: Position, order and tokenwise normalization
lessons.outcome: Explain why content attention alone does not identify position and preserve causal normalization.
lessons.lab: Jointly permute Q, K and V for unmasked content-only attention, then add a fixed position table. Separately compare tokenwise LayerNorm with sequence-wide normalization under causal-prefix checks.
lessons.verification: Without positions or a causal mask, jointly permuting inputs permutes outputs. A causal mask itself imposes an order boundary. Sequence-wide normalization can change earlier prefix values and is rejected for this decoder.

lessons.title: Multiple heads, residuals and a decoder block
lessons.outcome: Trace every dimension through a small decoder block and keep residual paths valid.
lessons.lab: Split a width 4 vector into two heads, rejoin it, apply a fixed feed-forward transformation and residual addition.
lessons.verification: Split/rejoin is an exact round trip; head width=2. Residual operands have the same shape, and every operation is tokenwise or causally masked.

lessons.title: Greedy decoding, temperature and sampling
lessons.outcome: Separate a distribution from the algorithm that selects a token.
lessons.lab: Use scores [2,1,0], fixed random draws and explicit tie rules; compare greedy choice with temperature and top-k filtering.
lessons.verification: Greedy chooses index 0; temperature changes probabilities but not this ranking. A fixed draw with a fixed cumulative table yields a reproducible choice.

lessons.title: A leakage audit before a model score
lessons.outcome: Identify target leakage, duplicate documents and test-set reuse independently of mask correctness.
lessons.lab: Split a fixed corpus by source document; compare shifted labels with copying the input as its own target and introduce one duplicate document.
lessons.verification: Inputs [2,5,7] pair with labels [5,7,3]; document sets are disjoint and the injected duplicate is detected. Prefix invariance alone does not establish these conditions.

lessons.title: Capstone: a small language-model evidence notebook
lessons.outcome: Present a count-based model and an independently tested attention mechanism with bounded claims.
lessons.lab: Fit a tiny bigram baseline from local text, freeze its tokenizer/split and produce causal-mask, loss and counterexample evidence.
lessons.verification: Conditional probabilities sum to 1, held-out units are declared, mask/prefix tests pass, and the report does not claim foundation-model competence.

lessons.title: PyTorch tensors and automatic gradients
lessons.outcome: Translate a NumPy calculation to tensors without requiring another deep-learning course.
lessons.lab: Derive 2*(w-2) with a finite-difference check, reproduce that squared-loss gradient in PyTorch CPU, and compare a fixed embedding lookup; inspect requires_grad and detach.
lessons.verification: For (w-2)^2 at w=0, gradient=-4. Detached values have no path to w, and the embedding output matches llm-008.

lessons.title: A tiny causal transformer from explicit parts
lessons.outcome: Assemble one decoder block and verify its shape and information boundary before training.
lessons.lab: Build a decoder with width 32, two heads, one block and vocabulary<=128; retain the NumPy mask test as a reference.
lessons.verification: Parameter count<50000, logits shape=(batch,time,vocabulary), and prefix outputs agree in eval mode within 1e-6.

lessons.title: Shifted batches, padding and token loss
lessons.outcome: Align inputs, targets and ignored padding without changing the evaluation denominator.
lessons.lab: Build inputs/labels from fixed token sequences and add ignored padding labels; compare sum/mean cross entropy over active targets.
lessons.verification: For [2,5,7,3], input=[2,5,7], target=[5,7,3]. Appending ignored targets changes neither the active count of 3 nor the mean loss.

lessons.title: A bounded training loop with visible state
lessons.outcome: Implement forward, loss, zero_grad, backward and optimizer.step in the correct order.
lessons.lab: Train on at most 128 local sequences for at most 200 steps; log an initial loss and a gradient norm on a fixed diagnostic batch.
lessons.verification: Weights change after a real step; gradients do not accumulate accidentally. All loss/gradient values remain finite, and stopped budgets are reported without a convergence claim.

lessons.title: Overfit one batch to diagnose the loop
lessons.outcome: Use a deliberately tiny overfit experiment to separate implementation failure from generalization.
lessons.lab: Repeat one fixed batch with dropout off; compare a no-update control and a functioning loop under the same declared step cap.
lessons.verification: The no-update control leaves weights identical. Record the observed loss curve and first failed invariant; do not interpret memorizing this batch as held-out quality.

lessons.title: Initialization and residual scale
lessons.outcome: Locate unstable activations and gradients without blaming data first.
lessons.lab: Compare a fixed small weight scale with an exaggerated scale on the same tiny batch; inspect finite norms and residual dimensions.
lessons.verification: The report contains layerwise activation/gradient norms and a named first nonfinite location if present. A claimed repair must restore finite output on the same input.

lessons.title: Document splits and contamination controls
lessons.outcome: Design a corpus split around the source unit and freeze it before model selection.
lessons.lab: Hash and deduplicate a hand-authored local corpus; add near-duplicate examples with known document-family IDs and construct grouped splits.
lessons.verification: No exact hash or family ID crosses train/validation/test. The original partition manifest is unchanged after evaluation.

lessons.title: Reproducibility, evaluation mode and restart
lessons.outcome: Distinguish repeatable inference from repeatable training and preserve optimizer state.
lessons.lab: Record seed/profile/dtype, disable dropout with model.eval(), and use Adam state plus model weights to compare an uninterrupted next update with a fresh-process restore on the same fixed batch.
lessons.verification: Eval-mode prefix tests pass with dropout disabled. Restored next-step tensors agree within 1e-6; cross-platform bitwise equality is not promised.

lessons.title: Top-p, termination and decoding failure cases
lessons.outcome: Implement a bounded decoder with explicit sampling and stop conditions.
lessons.lab: Use token probabilities [0.5,0.3,0.2], top-p=0.6 and a seeded CPU generator; add explicit EOS and maximum-length cases, retaining the threshold-crossing token.
lessons.verification: The retained nucleus contains the first two tokens, with original mass 0.8. Zero-temperature greedy mode is separate; output respects the token cap and EOS prevents a further token.

lessons.title: KV caches and incremental equivalence
lessons.outcome: Prove a cache optimization preserves the uncached causal computation.
lessons.lab: Run full-prefix and one-token-at-a-time inference on fixed weights, tracking position offsets and cache ownership by request.
lessons.verification: Per-position logits agree within 1e-6. A fresh request receives an empty cache; a deliberately reused foreign cache fails the isolation check.

lessons.title: Memory and compute without a GPU
lessons.outcome: Estimate attention and cache costs before choosing a context size.
lessons.lab: Count score elements and KV-cache bytes for declared T,H,dtype; compare T=16 and 32 while model width stays fixed.
lessons.verification: Doubling context quadruples the T-by-T score count and doubles KV storage. State exclusions such as allocator overhead and batching.

lessons.title: What a representation probe establishes
lessons.outcome: Distinguish accessible information from a causal explanation of a model decision.
lessons.lab: Probe frozen tiny-model representations on a synthetic local label with a shuffled-label control and a held-out document split.
lessons.verification: Report the control result and split unit. Even a successful probe is not described as proof that the model used that feature causally.

lessons.title: Calibration and comparable evaluation
lessons.outcome: Report predictive confidence under an explicit scoring and grouping policy.
lessons.lab: Compute token-weighted loss, a small calibration table and paired errors for fixed saved predictions; contrast a tokenizer change.
lessons.verification: Bins report counts, confidence and observed frequency; empty bins are explicit. Token losses across incompatible vocabularies are not directly ranked.

lessons.title: Capstone: train and audit a tiny transformer
lessons.outcome: Defend a bounded local training run with a frozen corpus and diagnostic evidence.
lessons.lab: Train a decoder with fewer than 50000 parameters, context at most 32 and at most 200 updates; compare held-out loss with the count baseline and submit failure analysis.
lessons.verification: Tokenizer/split/model hashes, masks, loss denominator, seed/profile and exact step count are recorded. Any quality conclusion names the held-out unit and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Scaling laws and the limits of a toy experiment
lessons.outcome: Interpret a scaling claim without extrapolating a tiny classroom fit to frontier systems.
lessons.lab: Read a supplied small loss-versus-compute table and identify which constants, data distributions and budgets changed between runs.
lessons.verification: Every comparison controls or labels parameter count, data and steps. The report explicitly refuses a frontier-performance prediction from the toy table.

lessons.title: Pretraining data provenance and evaluation contamination
lessons.outcome: Specify provenance and removal policies before training or evaluating on collected text.
lessons.lab: Build a manifest for local authored snippets with source, permission, split and duplicate-family fields; analyze a benchmark-answer contamination case.
lessons.verification: All fixture documents have provenance and a split. Benchmark answers and derived paraphrases are excluded from the training/selection source set.

lessons.title: Instruction tuning and loss masks
lessons.outcome: Explain how a supervised objective changes when only answer tokens receive loss.
lessons.lab: Use short fixed instruction/answer records with independent literal logits; compare full-sequence and answer-only loss masks and their direct logit gradients.
lessons.verification: The answer-only denominator equals the number of answer targets, not prompt+answer length. Evaluation tasks are held out by template family.

lessons.title: Low-rank adaptation without a package download
lessons.outcome: Derive and test a low-rank update while keeping base weights frozen.
lessons.lab: Use base W=I8, x=ones(8), target=zeros(8), A=ones((8,2))/8 and B=zeros((2,8)); form W+A@B and take one squared-loss SGD update of the adapter only.
lessons.verification: A and B have 32 parameters versus 64 in W. At initialization, zero delta matches the base. On the first step B changes, A may have zero gradient, and frozen W stays unchanged.

lessons.title: Preference objectives and what they do not prove
lessons.outcome: Compute a preference loss and separate preference evidence from factual correctness.
lessons.lab: Calculate a DPO-style logistic loss from fixed policy/reference log probabilities; reverse chosen/rejected labels and inspect the change.
lessons.verification: Equal preference margins produce log(2); swapping labels reverses the margin. No online RL, reward model service or factuality guarantee is claimed.

lessons.title: Precision and quantization error budgets
lessons.outcome: Measure a toy quantization tradeoff rather than claiming universal compression quality.
lessons.lab: Quantize W=[[0.1,-0.9],[1.7,-0.2]] with signed int8, maximum-absolute scales per tensor and per row, and nearest-even rounding; compare dequantized outputs on x=[1,-2].
lessons.verification: Retain the full-precision output [1.9,2.1]. Report scales, byte-storage assumptions, maximum absolute output error and saturation count for each policy; one fixture does not establish universal quality.

lessons.title: Inference scheduling and cache isolation
lessons.outcome: Keep request ownership and stop conditions correct when batching inference.
lessons.lab: Interleave two tiny requests with different prefix lengths; compare batched output with independent inference and invalidate caches on model/tokenizer version changes.
lessons.verification: Each request matches its independent logits within 1e-6 and retains its own token cap. Cache keys include model, tokenizer and request identity.

lessons.title: Retrieval: what RAG changes and what it cannot supply
lessons.outcome: Separate retrieval coverage from generation faithfulness and model knowledge.
lessons.lab: Rank a fixed six-document corpus for answerable and unanswerable questions; include a missing-evidence case and a malicious-looking document string as data.
lessons.verification: Report retrieval recall@k against authored relevance labels. The missing-evidence question remains unanswered; text instructions in documents never become actions.

lessons.title: Evaluate retrieval and answers separately
lessons.outcome: Identify whether an observed failure came from retrieval, reasoning or unsupported citation.
lessons.lab: Score saved retrieval results and deterministic answer records with document IDs and claim spans; compare an oracle-context control.
lessons.verification: A table separately counts retrieval misses, unsupported claims, incorrect answers and appropriate abstentions, keyed by question ID.

lessons.title: Tools, structured output and trust boundaries
lessons.outcome: Represent a tool request as untrusted data and require a separate authorization boundary.
lessons.lab: Validate fixed JSON proposals against a tiny allowlist; include unknown tools, path traversal and injected instructions in retrieved text.
lessons.verification: Only the declared read-only fixture operation is accepted as data. Unknown fields/operations and unsafe paths are rejected; no process, shell or external service is invoked.

lessons.title: Robustness, fairness and finite safety evidence
lessons.outcome: Turn a broad safety claim into a scoped test plan with explicit missing coverage.
lessons.lab: Analyze fixed adversarial, subgroup and counterfactual prompt families; separate an observed pass from a guarantee.
lessons.verification: Every result reports family, group, count and severity. Zero observed failures is not described as zero risk; no private/personally identifying data is collected.

lessons.title: A statistical evaluation and reliability argument
lessons.outcome: Choose paired units and uncertainty before comparing complete systems.
lessons.lab: Compare two fixed system result tables by question family using paired resampling; keep prompt and retrieval tuning on validation only.
lessons.verification: Pairs retain the same question IDs, repeated paraphrases remain in their family, and a final holdout is used once. The report includes failures and an abstention policy.

lessons.title: Optional framework comparison without a second prerequisite
lessons.outcome: Translate attention contracts without requiring TensorFlow to complete the LLM route.
lessons.lab: Map shapes, weight layouts, mask polarity and training/evaluation flags between NumPy, PyTorch and documented Keras APIs; optionally run TensorFlow only if separately prepared.
lessons.verification: The worksheet names API-specific boolean-mask meanings and exact weight/layout assumptions. TensorFlow execution is explicitly optional and absent from llm-042 prerequisites.

lessons.title: Capstone: a defensible language-system decision
lessons.outcome: Recommend a bounded system only when its evidence and operating limits support the intended use.
lessons.lab: Compare the tiny transformer, count baseline and a local retrieval variant on frozen questions; deliver reproducible artifacts, trust-boundary tests and a reviewer-facing decision.
lessons.verification: Acceptance requires lineage/split hashes, paired held-out results, mask/cache tests, latency/token budgets, failure examples and an explicit go/no-go with limitations. A no-go is a valid evidence-based result.

lessons.title: Encoder, decoder and encoder-decoder architectures and objectives
lessons.outcome: Transformer architecture describes which positions exchange information and how those representations are used.
lessons.lab: Use zero queries/keys and values[[2, 0], [0, 2], [6, 6]] under all-allowed and causal masks.
lessons.verification: encoder rows all[8/3, 8/3]; decoder rows[2, 0], [1, 1], [8/3, 8/3]. both cross outputs[1, 1]; padded source weight 0.

lessons.title: RoPE, relative positions, ALiBi and long-context limits
lessons.outcome: Position mechanisms tell attention how token order or distance should influence a comparison.
lessons.lab: Rotate[1, 0] bypi/2 and check length preservation.
lessons.verification: approximately[0, 1]; norm 1. finite vector; long_context_quality_verified=False; odd width rejected.

lessons.title: Pre/post normalization, RMSNorm and gated feed-forward networks
lessons.outcome: Normalization placement changes the residual network's gradient path.
lessons.lab: Normalize vector 3, 4] with unit gain and epsilon 1e-8.
lessons.verification: RMSNorm mean nonzero; LayerNorm mean approximately 0. LayerNorm shift invariant; RMSNorm changes; both zero cases finite.

lessons.title: MHA, MQA, GQA and blockwise exact attention
lessons.outcome: Attention architecture and attention execution are separate design dimensions.
lessons.lab: Use batch 1, time 5, query heads 4, head width 2, float32, and compare KV heads 4, 2, 1.
lessons.verification: raw KV bytes 320, 160, 80; projection weights 256, 192, 160 for model width 8 without biases. both raise ValueError; no output NaNs are accepted.

lessons.title: Sparse experts, routing capacity and load balancing
lessons.outcome: A mixture-of-experts layer routes each token to a subset of specialized transformations.
lessons.lab: Use experts I, 2I, -I and three token/router rows with selected probabilities 3/4 and 1/4.
lessons.verification: outputs[1.25, 0], [0, 1.75], [-.25, -.25]. invalid policies raise ValueError; top-2 tie indices 0, 1.

lessons.title: Exact speculative decoding and cache rollback
lessons.outcome: Speculative decoding proposes several tokens with a cheaper draft model and verifies them against a target model.
lessons.lab: Use p[.5, .3, .2] and q[.2, .5, .3]; calculate accepted mass, rejection mass and residual.
lessons.verification: accepted mass[.2, .3, .2]; rejection .3; residual[1, 0, 0]; combined mass p. rejection mass is 0 and residual is None; accepted EOS stops generation; the token cap is respected; unsupported proposals raise ValueError.

capstones.title: A language-model evidence notebook
capstones.brief: Use local counts and attention invariants to distinguish implementation evidence from a broad model claim.
deliverables: fixed document split and NLL/perplexity worksheet
causal-mask tests and a leakage counterexample
acceptance: Token and document denominators are declared.
Prefix invariance and malformed-mask checks pass.
No online model or pretrained asset is needed.

capstones.title: A tiny transformer under a hard budget
capstones.brief: Train and inspect one CPU decoder on a small local corpus.
acceptance: Training, selection and test documents are disjoint.
Fresh inference and cache equivalence match within 1e-6.
A completed budget is not reported as proof of useful generalization.

capstones.title: A defensible language-system decision
capstones.brief: Compare bounded alternatives and recommend a system or a justified no-go.
deliverables: resource manifest, limitations and go/no-go rationale
acceptance: No test-set prompt tuning or document-family leakage occurs.
Claims cite the evaluation unit and preserve paired samples.
Unsupported answers, missing retrieval and unsafe tool proposals are counted separately.
No TensorFlow installation or hosted service is required.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.supports: Scaled dot-product attention, positional information, multihead composition and decoder masking; the course adds independent causal invariants.

sources.title: PyTorch scaled dot-product attention
sources.supports: API-specific mask polarity, causal behavior and explicit dropout_p control. The stable alias resolved to 2.14 at review; this is not a dependency upgrade request.

sources.title: PyTorch cross entropy
sources.supports: Class-index targets, ignore_index and reduction semantics.

sources.title: Subword units with byte pair encoding
sources.supports: Subword segmentation by learned merge operations; training-only vocabulary fitting is an explicit course evaluation rule.

sources.title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
sources.supports: Nucleus sampling as a decoding method, not a correctness guarantee.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.supports: Retrieval plus generation as distinct mechanisms; retrieval does not establish answer support by itself.

sources.title: LoRA
sources.supports: Low-rank adaptation with a frozen base; the course uses a tiny explicit matrix experiment.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization
sources.supports: Preference loss relative to a reference policy; preference optimization is not proof of factual accuracy.

sources.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
sources.supports: Controlled parameter/data/compute tradeoffs and the limits of extrapolating classroom experiments.
